items.title: LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI
items.summary: LVMH's Media Division and OpenAI announced a partnership to support journalism with AI and make LVMH publications more accessible through ChatGPT.
items.why: Shows publishers distributing content through ChatGPT, a pattern relevant to enterprise content licensing and integration strategy.

items.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
items.summary: An arXiv paper finds that hard-filtering stale facts in LLM memory systems can reduce accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts.
items.why: Engineers building agent memory should note that aggressive deletion of stale facts can hurt accuracy when classification is unreliable.

items.title: Does the Ranking Hold? A Practitioner-Facing Audit of Hallucination Detectors on Small, Quantized, On-Device LLMs
items.summary: An arXiv audit evaluates four hallucination detectors on small, 4-bit quantized on-device LLMs such as Phi-3-mini and Gemma-2-2B.
items.why: Teams shipping small on-device models get practical evidence on whether existing hallucination detectors hold up outside large research models.

items.title: LoRAWeaver: Directional Adapter Routing in LoRA Representation Space
items.summary: LoRAWeaver is a training-free method that routes inference to LoRA adapters by treating routing as representation alignment in adapter-output space.
items.why: It offers a way to select among growing pools of LoRA adapters without retraining the router when new adapters are added.

items.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes tabular population priors as retrieval for predicting medication sets from EHR data, instead of retrieving similar patient records for an LLM.

items.title: An Operationalization of Opaque Serial Depth
items.summary: An arXiv paper operationalizes opaque serial depth, a proxy for how much unverbalized serial computation a model can perform without an interpretable bottleneck.
items.why: It bears on whether chain-of-thought remains a reliable oversight tool as architectures change.

items.title: Advancing Quantization for R&R Models with Microscaling Formats
items.summary: An arXiv paper examines microscaling number formats for quantizing recommendation and ranking models under a strict 0.01% Normalized Entropy quality margin.
items.why: Ad-ranking teams with tight quality bars need to know whether aggressive quantization can meet launch constraints without accuracy loss.

items.title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
items.summary: An arXiv study places Gemma 3 12B in a simulated London silver-fixing case and tests how gain, loss, blame and credit framings affect its willingness to collude.
items.why: It highlights that framing and pressure can shift long-horizon agent behavior toward market manipulation, a safety concern for deployed agents.

items.title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces model annealing, which spends remaining training budget on review and consolidation using memory of past model states and adversarial examples.

items.title: Astrocyte Biocomputing: Astrocytic Contributions to Neural Network Computation
items.summary: An arXiv paper discusses how astrocytes may contribute to neural network computation, learning, and memory in the brain.

items.title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents
items.summary: An arXiv paper frames powder X-ray diffraction structure determination as a verifiable agentic search problem and introduces pXRD-Bench with 200 simulated problems.
items.why: Provides a verifiable benchmark design for LLM agents in scientific tasks where candidate answers can be checked during inference.

items.title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces AI-Voyager, a public-interest system where residents and AI together read, contest and draft revisions to government AI rules.

items.title: When Does Less Information Pay? An Exact Finite Atlas of Representation, Payoff, and Cost
items.summary: An arXiv paper enumerates representations in a four-state world to show when retaining less information can still solve a task as well as richer representations.

items.title: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.summary: An arXiv paper synthesizes 516 multi-agent LLM configurations to separate the effects of coordination, ensembling, and test-time compute on accuracy.
items.why: Multi-agent gains may come mostly from extra samples or compute rather than coordination, which affects how teams benchmark agent architectures.

items.title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters
items.summary: An arXiv paper studies using an LLM to decide when and how to evolve behavioral clusters as user or item patterns drift over time.
items.why: Offers an alternative to fixed threshold triggers and refit-and-track rules for maintaining evolving clusterings in production systems.

items.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit
items.summary: An arXiv paper audits safety side effects of preventative persona steering, which adds persona vectors during fine-tuning to suppress traits like sycophancy and hallucination.
items.why: Engineers using activation steering to curb model traits should check whether preventative steering introduces unintended safety regressions before adopting it.

items.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
items.summary: Researchers introduced AscendGYM, a benchmark of 48 kernels on Ascend NPUs testing whether agents can optimize existing kernels using real-workload input configurations.
items.why: Teams optimizing LLM workloads on Ascend hardware get a realistic benchmark for evaluating agent-driven kernel optimization.

items.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions
items.summary: A paper proposes treating generated evaluation suites for LLM agents as diversity-driven search, injecting controlled defects into a tau-squared-bench agent to test regression detection.
items.why: It suggests a better way to build agent regression suites than scoring them by mean pass rate, which discards search results.

items.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say
items.summary: A paper uses presupposition theory to study when LLM agents act on false assumptions about tool outputs versus user statements before cancelling reservations or deleting files.
items.why: Agents taking irreversible actions need checks that verify tool-observed facts against user claims before acting, not after.

items.title: Learn then Bet: Learning Interpretable Rules for Reliable Agent Intervention
items.summary: Researchers introduce LeBet, a statistical framework that learns interpretable rules for deciding when to stop, upgrade, or assist long-running autonomous agents.
items.why: Replacing crude turn limits and keyword filters with learned intervention rules could reduce both wrongly stopped and wrongly continued agent runs.

items.title: Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified? A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: A benchmark of 1,762 text-window pairs tests how multimodal forecasting models use text that aligns, conflicts with, or is unrelated to sensed time series.
items.why: Shows whether forecasting models with text inputs actually weigh conflicting text reliably, which matters for AIoT deployments.

items.title: OCTAVE: A Capability-Resolved Benchmark for End-to-End HTML5 Game Generation
items.summary: OCTAVE is a benchmark of 180 tasks for end-to-end HTML5 game generation, scoring eight capability dimensions across PC Web, Mobile Web, 2D, and 3D.
items.why: Capability-level scoring shows which parts of game generation agents implement and which requirements they miss, beyond one aggregate score.

items.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
items.summary: Co-Sight Harness moves workflow definitions and domain knowledge into versioned control assets enforced by a state machine and acceptance gates, keeping the language model fixed.
items.why: Externalizing workflow state and gates offers a way to make long business agent workflows more reliable without changing the model.

items.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
items.summary: ChlCast is an AI model that produces daily high-resolution forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a, reported to outperform the operational global biogeochemical system.

items.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
items.summary: A cross-linguistic study examines acoustic biomarkers for cognitive impairment across interactive and single-speaker speech tasks in multiple languages.

items.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
items.summary: A paper proposes federated soft poly-level learning, extending multi-level optimization beyond bilevel and trilevel to four or more hierarchical levels over distributed networks, with convergence guarantees.
items.why: Offers theoretical convergence guarantees for hierarchical optimization across distributed nodes, though practical impact is still early.

items.title: A Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization in Model Merging
items.summary: A spectral framework is proposed for universal proxy regularization in model merging, aiming to replace task data with a task-agnostic proxy distribution to reduce parameter interference.
items.why: If a task-agnostic proxy suffices, model merging could avoid sharing other tasks' data, preserving the independence and privacy the method assumes.

items.title: Knowledge After Collapse: Context and Wording Shape Factual Accessibility in Language Models
items.summary: Knowledge Answer Divergence, an evaluation protocol, tests how language models adopt, persist with, or recover from false corrections in factual conversations.
items.why: Shows that conversation history and wording can change whether models keep false answers, which affects reliability in multi-turn applications.

items.title: Certified Improvements to Best-Known Thomson-Problem Configurations with a Search Pipeline Built with Large Language Model Agents
items.summary: An LLM-agent search pipeline produced certified configurations for Thomson problem instances N=912, 1382 and 2502 with lower energies than Cambridge Cluster Database values.

items.title: TReC: Evaluating Move-Induced State Changes in Instruction-Conditioned Go
items.summary: TReC, a metric, compares how a predicted Go move and the expert move change a board-state embedding in a frozen KataGo network, using cosine similarity over 680 positions.
items.why: Offers a board-state-aware alternative to coordinate distance for evaluating game-playing model moves.

items.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system designed to automate reinforcement learning training.
items.why: Automating RL training could reduce the manual supervision needed for stabilizing and iterating on model training pipelines.

items.title: MASTARS: Multi-Agent Sequential Trajectory Augmentation with Return-Conditioned Subgoals
items.summary: Researchers present MASTARS, a diffusion-based method for augmenting offline multi-agent reinforcement learning trajectories while balancing diversity and coordination.
items.why: It targets a known limit of offline multi-agent RL, where fixed datasets constrain performance, offering a data augmentation approach.

items.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study
items.summary: A study stress-tests a median-based GPU rental price benchmark under simulated missing marketplace quotes and evaluates recovery methods.
items.why: Teams relying on GPU price indices should know how missing quotes affect coverage and error in published benchmarks.

items.title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding
items.summary: Researchers propose Vision-as-a-Tool, a framework that gives text-only coding agents visual perception through external tools rather than relying on the model's own vision.
items.why: Decoupling perception into tools could help agentic coding systems evaluate generated UI artifacts beyond the base model's vision limits.

items.title: Can Agents Keep Up with Time? An Empirical Analysis of Temporal Adaptation After a Conversational Hiatus
items.summary: An empirical study examines whether long-horizon agents adapt to time passing during a conversational hiatus, when scheduled events lapse but records stay unchanged.
items.why: Persistent assistants that act on stale state after time gaps could make wrong scheduling decisions, so evaluations need time-awareness.

items.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
items.summary: Researchers propose G-CAST, a governed continual self-training approach for LLM shopping agents facing shifting user demands and evolving tools.
items.why: Production agents whose tools and user needs change over time need governed retraining to avoid drift; the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Causally Constrained and Uncertainty-Aware Cardiopulmonary Risk Prediction
items.summary: Researchers present CE-Agent, a causally constrained, uncertainty-aware model that predicts lung cancer and cardiovascular risk from routine chest CT.
items.why: Combining CT findings across diseases with uncertainty estimates targets clinical risk tools that currently evaluate each disease separately.

items.title: Aligning AI Teams
items.summary: Researchers investigate why safety alignment on individual LLM agents fails to transfer to multi-agent teams and test interventions to preserve it.
items.why: Single-agent safety testing may not carry over to multi-agent deployments, so teams should evaluate safety at the team level.

items.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
items.summary: A study tests whether direction-based abliteration and ARA can still remove refusal from newer open-weight LLMs compared with their predecessors.
items.why: Results show refusal removal is not uniformly getting harder, relevant for teams assessing safety robustness of open-weight model releases.

items.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process
items.summary: Researchers present DECODE, a method for diagnosing whether failures in LLM-based automated interpretability stem from extracted representations or from explanation generation.
items.why: Self-referential LLM interpretation pipelines without ground truth raise reliability concerns that engineers evaluating such tools need to diagnose.

items.title: AI-aided Decision-Making in Education - Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility
items.summary: A paper examines how AI-aided decision-making in education raises issues of uncertainty, explainability, and human responsibility.

items.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Researchers propose FlexCast, a time series foundation model framework that separates variable-context conditioning from autoregressive prediction to clarify sources of generalization.
items.why: Disentangling training and inference factors could guide design choices for time series forecasting models.

items.title: OmniScore-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Musical Score Reading
items.summary: Researchers introduce OmniScore-Bench, a benchmark of 3,000 questions testing vision-language models on musical score reading across six aspects.
items.why: It separates recognition, structure, and meaning in VLM score reading, showing where models fail beyond transcription accuracy.

items.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce Soteria, a framework combining formally verified hierarchical planning with runtime enforcement to balance task completion and safety for LLM agents.
items.why: It addresses the tension where blocking unsafe tool calls can strand agents, offering a way to keep both utility and policy compliance.

items.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
items.summary: Researchers show adversarial changes to symbolic vocabulary can expose weaknesses in LLM planners that lack commonsense cues.
items.why: LLM planners that depend on naming cues may be unreliable under obfuscated task definitions, which matters for agent deployments.

items.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
items.summary: SWIFT proposes sample-wise instance fine-tuning that adapts time-series forecasting foundation models using each target instance's own history, without needing an extra dataset.
items.why: It removes the need for an additional fine-tuning dataset, a practical hurdle for adopting forecasting foundation models.

items.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose semantic strategy unlearning for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, so teams can drop a learned coordination convention when deployment requirements change.
items.why: Learned multi-agent conventions can become obsolete or unsafe after requirement changes, and this offers a way to remove them.

items.title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
items.summary: RecMem compresses long user interaction histories into fixed memory slots using recurrent memory, aiming to make generative recommendation over long sequences cheaper.
items.why: Processing cost in generative recommenders grows with history length, so fixed-size memory compression could cut serving costs.

items.title: What Balanced Accuracy Cannot Identify in Neural-Signal Decoding under Test-Time Adaptation
items.summary: A paper examines how balanced accuracy and aggregate metrics can miss subject-level effects when test-time adaptation is applied to neural-signal decoding across EEG and ECG datasets.
items.why: Aggregate metrics can hide per-subject behavior changes, which matters when evaluating adaptive models on medical signal data.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100
items.summary: The study measures latency and paper-retrieval success for eight open-weight LLMs on a Mac Studio and a two-A100 server, with context lengths up to 128k tokens.
items.why: It gives concrete latency and retrieval tradeoffs for running local LLM research assistants instead of hosted APIs.

items.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
items.summary: OutfitterBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon resource allocation and keeping their own commitments feasible as opportunities change.
items.why: It targets agent failures in sustained operations, such as overcommitting capacity, that short-horizon benchmarks miss.

items.title: Tracing Actual Causes with Counterfactual Witness Maps
items.summary: The paper introduces counterfactual witness maps, a sound and complete enumeration procedure for finding all Halpernian actual causes in acyclic structural causal models.
items.why: Complete cause enumeration is a prerequisite for downstream responsibility and blame assessment, though the work is theoretical.

items.title: Measured from the feed: the unsustainable growth of AI video generation
items.summary: The authors measured yearly video output of two commercial text-to-video platforms and project that emissions could rise nearly seventy-five-fold under continued growth.
items.why: Engineering and leadership teams deploying generative video should weigh energy growth against efficiency gains.

items.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation
items.summary: Researchers train a single RF source separator across many signal and interference pairs, rather than one specialized separator per pair, to handle unseen interference.
items.why: Specialized separators often fail on unseen interference, so a generalist separator addresses a real limitation for jammed receivers.

items.title: The Transformer Paradigm: Dynamic Processing and a New Principle of Inference
items.summary: A theoretical paper argues the Transformer represents a new inference paradigm in which some transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input.

items.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
items.summary: WebArena-Pro is a reproducible benchmark for web agents spanning more heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows than prior benchmarks.
items.why: Broader and reproducible web-agent evaluation helps teams compare agents on realistic multi-app browser work.

items.title: TotalSegmentator Aorta Report: Automated Aortic Diameter Measurement at 11 Standardized Landmarks on CT Images
items.summary: An open-source tool automatically measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks on CT angiography, evaluated on 239 examinations from a single center.
items.why: An open-source automated measurement tool could standardize aortic reporting in clinical imaging pipelines.

items.title: Interactive deep-learning based interface for brain tumour segmentation
items.summary: An interactive deep-learning interface for brain tumour segmentation from MR images is presented, aimed at reducing catastrophic errors on varied MR sequences.

items.title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap
items.summary: LACCO is a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global gradient communication with computation for training language models over low-bandwidth networks.
items.why: Reducing synchronization stalls in low-bandwidth distributed training could lower cost for teams training across slow networks.

items.title: Understanding the limits of snapshot-based fault diagnosis in distribution networks
items.summary: The paper separates error sources in snapshot-based fault diagnosis on distribution networks, testing three IEEE feeders and a public dataset with distributed generation.
items.why: Shows which factors limit fault classifier accuracy, informing when cheap snapshot-based screening can be trusted in grid operations.

items.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
items.summary: Researchers propose A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that splits pipeline stages between edge devices and a server, with a complete on-device fallback.
items.why: It shows how to keep embedded voice agents responsive and working during network outages, relevant to edge AI system design.

items.title: Two-Clustering Regime of Token Dynamics in Causal Attention
items.summary: A paper proves that causal attention token dynamics converge to two clusters when the largest eigenvalue of the value transformation is positive, and shows the conjecture fails otherwise.

items.title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents
items.summary: A preregistered experiment with 420 teams of three AI agents tested whether agents learn rule-breaking behavior from peers via randomized assignment.

items.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers
items.summary: Researchers present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures to minimize total energy consumption.

items.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
items.summary: JFinBench is introduced as a Japanese financial benchmark of 321 examples from 2026 certification exams, designed to be continuously refreshed.
items.why: Engineers evaluating LLMs for finance in Japan get a country-specific, regularly updatable test set that reduces training-data leakage risk.

items.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.summary: Researchers develop a large language model-based intelligent agent for adaptive fast-charging control of lithium-ion batteries.

items.title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models
items.summary: The paper derives sharp analytic bounds on probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models with binary treatments and outcomes.

items.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
items.summary: Researchers map LLM token generation onto a similarity network built from input embeddings of six open LLMs, finding a scale-free but fragmented topology.

items.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
items.summary: The article argues that using AI judges to select prompts or train clinical AI models turns evaluation into intervention, and calls for independent clinical testing.
items.why: Teams using LLM-as-judge to tune clinical systems risk optimizing for errors the judge misses, so independent validation is needed.

items.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
items.summary: The paper introduces MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts model for cross-database generalization that aims to match gains from large pretraining with less data.

items.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: Researchers propose a causally-aware deep learning framework with defensive variational autoencoders for secure mmWave beam alignment resistant to adversarial perturbations.

items.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
items.summary: VLAN is a vision-language navigation benchmark with 1,000 scenes and 20K trajectories, providing embodiment-specific accessibility labels for legged and wheeled robots.

items.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling
items.summary: VelServe proposes tail-calibrated scheduling to reduce decode jitter in LLM inference and meet time-between-tokens latency SLOs in serving systems.
items.why: Decode jitter causes many SLO violations in long streaming responses, so tail-aware scheduling directly affects serving reliability.

items.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators
items.summary: A resilience analysis of smart home agents across simulated full power outages finds they are capable but behave unpredictably as grid operators.

items.title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
items.summary: LeCat is a two-part framework that measures how LLMs learn category knowledge from pretraining data, covering memorization, generalization, and flexible use.

items.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
items.summary: Researchers extend the SleepXAI framework to compare five explainability methods for single-channel EEG sleep staging, checking attributions against AASM frequency bands.
items.why: Interpretable sleep staging could ease clinical adoption of automated models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
items.summary: Researchers propose Support-Gated World-Model decision support, which withholds simulated patient responses to vasopressor doses when the data gives insufficient support.
items.why: It shows a way for LLM agents to flag unreliable simulations in high-stakes settings instead of acting on them unchecked.

items.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
items.summary: Researchers frame wrist sEMG keystroke decoding as a live problem constrained by muscle signals, language, and typing behaviour, not only offline character error rate.
items.why: Treating typing behaviour and language as constraints may matter for building usable real-time neural input interfaces.

items.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
items.summary: ARCHER is a two-stage training framework that teaches small language models to produce executable, calculator-grounded reasoning traces for math tasks.
items.why: Executable, auditable reasoning could make small local models more reliable for math-heavy tasks where privacy or cost rules out large hosted models.

items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.summary: A case study applies mechanistic interpretability to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to explain why web agents hallucinate actions unavailable on a live website.
items.why: It tests whether interpretability tools can diagnose real agent failures, a gap engineers debugging web agents would care about.

items.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
items.summary: A theoretical study models how evolutionary selection shapes AI agents' tradeoffs between task completion and rules of conduct, and whether experience aligns choices with human judgments.
items.why: The text is theoretical and gives little concrete guidance for engineers building agents today.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.summary: ModHarness-RL treats the agent harness, the scaffold deciding what the model sees and receives, as learnable programs that evolve during agentic reinforcement learning.
items.why: Learned, evolving harnesses could replace hand-written scaffolds that stay fixed during agent RL training.

items.title: HARDTESTGEN: A High-Quality RL Verifier Generation Pipeline for LLM Algorithmic Coding
items.summary: HARDTESTGEN is a pipeline that synthesizes high-quality test cases to build reliable reward verifiers for reinforcement learning on algorithmic coding problems.
items.why: Stronger verifiers reduce reward hacking from wrong code that passes weak tests, which matters for training code-generation models.

items.title: PhysDox: Benchmarking LLMs on Physical Feasibility Auditing of Physiological Sensing Protocols
items.summary: PhysDox is a benchmark testing whether LLMs can audit physiological sensing protocols for physical feasibility, classifying severity and diagnosing fatal constraint violations.
items.why: It shows LLM-generated experimental protocols can be fluent yet physically infeasible, a risk for teams using LLMs in lab design.

items.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
items.summary: Researchers compare classical and hybrid quantum-classical sequence models for positron energy regression on the public CaloGAN calorimeter shower dataset.
items.why: The text gives limited detail on outcomes, so its practical relevance to most engineering teams is unclear.

items.title: ProdPilot: A Layered Model Context Protocol System for Automated Production Readiness and Deployment of Vibe-Coded Projects
items.summary: ProdPilot is a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and related vibe-coded projects for production readiness issues like hardcoded credentials and missing health endpoints.
items.why: Automated checks for deployment defects in AI-generated apps address a common failure point when prototypes first reach production.

items.title: Time-Consistent Evaluation of Hierarchical Code Graphs for SWE Agents
items.summary: The paper evaluates repository-aware software engineering agents on DragonFly and React using repository snapshots and knowledge graphs locked at historical commits to prevent leakage.
items.why: Zero-leakage evaluation protocols give a more trustworthy measure of coding agent performance than standard contaminated benchmarks.

items.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms
items.summary: The paper proposes a verifiable structure for specifying which predicate supports a high-level object in generative modeling, and bounds error in null-support regions.
items.why: The text is highly theoretical and offers little direct relevance to most engineering or leadership decisions.

items.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function
items.summary: Researchers designed lanmodulin variants for rare earth element binding and found that structural confidence did not predict measured metal-binding function across 297 designs.
items.why: Structural confidence scores alone are a poor selection filter, so function-guided screening is needed in protein design pipelines.

items.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: An empirical study tests whether LLMs can use weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks by directly modifying their weights.
items.why: LLMs that can edit model weights create a new supply-chain security risk that teams deploying third-party models should account for.

items.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
items.summary: Researchers propose WETW, a method that learns pair-specific weighted Euclidean distances to approximate Dynamic Time Warping for faster similarity search over long time series.
items.why: Offers a potentially cheaper alternative to quadratic-cost DTW for searching large collections of misaligned time series.

items.title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
items.summary: Researchers analyzed 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 coding-agent configurations, using a rule-based parser to map traces to high-level actions beyond binary task success.
items.why: Suggests benchmarks that score only pass/fail hide behaviors behind agent outcomes, which matters when evaluating coding agents.

items.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
items.summary: Researchers study budget-conditioned object search for vision-language-navigation agents, where the agent is given an explicit action budget and must find as many target instances as possible.

items.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce Diffusion Tree Sampling, a Monte Carlo tree search over the denoising trajectory, to steer crystal generative models toward multiple properties at inference time.
items.why: Offers a way to adapt pretrained generative models to new objectives without fine-tuning a new model for each one.

items.title: Use-case-driven ontology modeling with the NeOn methodology for ambient assisted living
items.summary: Researchers present an ontology built with the NeOn methodology as the semantic data layer of the Virtual Home Framework for ambient assisted living in smart homes.

items.title: Do Mixture-of-Experts Routers Benefit from Ensembling?
items.summary: Researchers evaluate applying ensembling to the routing step of mixture-of-experts models, using an ensemble of routers trained jointly with the experts to propose expert weights.
items.why: Explores whether ensemble gains transfer to MoE routing, a design choice relevant to building sparse models.

items.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
items.summary: Researchers evaluate image-specific and image-agnostic adversarial attacks on detectors in tracking-by-detection systems, measuring their effect on vehicle trajectory estimation in autonomous driving.
items.why: Shows detection accuracy alone does not capture how adversarial image perturbations degrade downstream tracking in autonomous vehicles.

items.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent
items.summary: Researchers show that attacks which failed against frontier models in isolation can break multi-agent systems such as Codex and Claude Code under specific circumstances.
items.why: Indicates per-model safety testing may miss vulnerabilities that only emerge when models operate as part of multi-agent systems.

items.title: GraphScent: Calibrating Directional Relevance Signals for Bounded-Context Code Localization
items.summary: Researchers study directional relevance signals for code localization with Gemma 4 models on 211 Python issues, aiming to run stateless repository localization on a single consumer GPU.
items.why: Points toward practical local coding assistants that avoid long multi-turn exploration histories on consumer hardware.

items.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes
items.summary: Researchers present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes, built from a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production.

items.title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
items.summary: Researchers define dialectical competence, the ability of a language model to hold a correct position under contested answers and yield only to better reasoning, and show it differs from accuracy.
items.why: Highlights that first-answer accuracy does not measure whether models resist wrong pushback, a gap relevant to deployed assistants.

items.title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling
items.summary: Researchers find that widely used text-to-image reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning tests, and that preference fine-tuning can erode these capabilities.
items.why: Suggests reward models used for selection and RL post-training may fail on attribute binding, relations and counting, affecting image pipelines.

items.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
items.summary: AGIBOT presents X-Nav, a system that takes a bipedal humanoid robot through a language-instructed long-horizon navigation mission from indoors to outdoors.
items.why: Demonstrates end-to-end data-to-deployment navigation on a humanoid, a benchmark for embodied robotics engineering.

items.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
items.summary: Researchers propose a training-free acceleration for multi-view 3D transformers like VGGT by approximating global attention differently per layer role, based on analysis across seven datasets.
items.why: Offers a no-retraining speedup for quadratic attention cost in multi-image 3D reconstruction models.

items.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator that generates audio-grounded rationales before scoring text relevance and audio quality for text-to-audio generation.
items.why: Provides an explainable automatic judge that could reduce reliance on slow human evaluation when iterating on audio models.

items.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks
items.summary: Researchers study whether Weightless Neural Networks, such as WiSARD, are robust to adversarial examples, finding that binarization thresholds can still let perturbations change predictions.
items.why: Engineers deploying lightweight classifiers for intrusion detection should not assume binarization alone provides adversarial robustness.

items.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost
items.summary: Researchers show imitation policies for robot manipulation learn to discount noisy object-position readings by blending them with the robot's proprioceptive state, and give a predictive formula for this weighting.
items.why: Teams training robot policies on noisy perception can use this law to predict how much policies rely on sensor readings versus proprioception.

items.title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
items.summary: An LLM used as a coding agent with open-source tools wrote a job-shop scheduling solver that was compared against commercial solvers on large unsolved benchmark instances.
items.why: It shows agent-written heuristics can approach commercial optimization solvers on hard scheduling problems, though the reported solver still trailed the commercial ones on the headline instance.

items.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
items.summary: Researchers present a method for making LLM-based agentic forecasting systems produce logically consistent forecasts that satisfy probability axioms across related events.
items.why: Forecasts for related events that contradict each other undermine decision-making, so consistency enforcement matters for anyone using LLM forecasts operationally.

items.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference
items.summary: Superfluid, an open-source local LLM server, is presented for distributing inference across several machines from different vendors and serving multiple agents on one device.
items.why: Developers with several idle local machines could pool them to serve models privately without per-token cost.

items.title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework for brand-aware product redesign generation that uses a constructed brand image to keep text-to-image designs consistent with brand constraints.

items.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
items.summary: GDP_xlsx is a benchmark of 70 professional workplace spreadsheet requests across 13 domains, scored with expert rubrics and an agentic judge that opens the workbook.
items.why: It gives teams a rubric-based way to compare frontier models and agents on realistic spreadsheet tasks.

items.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
items.summary: Typhoon is an audiovisual art installation that prompts an LLM seeded with Joseph Conrad's novella to reflect on the current AI moment, using activation steering.

items.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model proposed as a fast first-pass system that could run on local hardware ahead of a slower LLM agent.
items.why: Offloading routine queries to local models could cut API costs and keep sensitive organizational queries off external APIs.

items.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling
items.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation using 3D feature grids, a quadratic-gating decoder, and a prediction-free sampler to speed up building video representations.
items.why: Faster construction of implicit video representations could make them practical for industrial video applications.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
items.summary: A multi-phase study evaluates whether LLMs can optimize pretrained YOLO26 detector weights gradient-free, comparing them against evolutionary methods and a random-policy control on COCO.
items.why: Results indicate whether LLM guidance adds value over standard search for weight editing of detectors, a question teams weighing that approach need answered.

items.title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions
items.summary: A multimodal person concept model is proposed that learns person identities from few observations without person labels, for robust identification by service robots under varying conditions.

items.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: CarryOn is a lightweight method that learns which parts of an agent's interaction history to keep in context for long-horizon LLM agent tasks.
items.why: Better context selection addresses the tradeoff between summaries that drop needed details and full histories that add noise in long agent runs.

items.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
items.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework that reuses scene-generation construction processes and experience across different game engine backends via a canonical scene context and backend adapters.
items.why: Separating world state from engine-specific adapters could reduce rework when moving generation pipelines between game engines.

items.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
items.summary: V-JEPA-LM is a video-language model approach aimed at letting language models use the dynamics captured by V-JEPA video encoders rather than only retrieving static, caption-aligned attributes.
items.why: It highlights that video-LM training can leave useful encoder dynamics unused, relevant to teams building video question-answering systems.

items.title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
items.summary: Researchers argue that errors in El Niño forecasts may originate from mesoscale errors in initial ocean-current states common to current models and observation systems.
items.why: It shows that small-scale initial-condition errors in ocean data can propagate into large-scale climate forecast uncertainty, relevant to anyone building or validating forecasting pipelines.

items.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries
items.summary: Researchers present an active-learning framework for LTLf that learns temporal logic specifications through learner-teacher interaction, aiming to avoid equivalence queries and restarted SAT searches.
items.why: Automatically learning temporal specifications could reduce the effort of writing verification and monitoring formulas, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
items.summary: A technical report compares fine-tuning recipes for UltraBERT-380M encoder models that select among options in one forward pass, reporting 69.7% to 72.1% test accuracy versus 67.6% for Qwen3-0.6B.
items.why: Smaller encoder models may match a much smaller LLM on option-selection tasks at lower inference cost, which matters for cost-sensitive deployments.

items.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
items.summary: DySENSE is a framework for generating dynamic, spatiotemporal urban energy data and emulating energy use using satellite imagery, aimed at future cities.

items.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
items.summary: A theoretical paper derives criteria for when sharing mixture-of-experts experts across layers or steps reduces local error and still helps final multi-step outputs.
items.why: It gives principled guidance on when expert sharing in MoE architectures improves end-to-end results rather than only local prediction error.

items.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
items.summary: Researchers propose classifying animal behavior by first reconstructing 3D body and object geometry from video, then classifying, demonstrated on simulated and real mouse video.

items.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design
items.summary: Researchers propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA) on multi-agent systems, where malicious agents optimize responses to skew the aggregated final solution, and study securing such systems by design.
items.why: Multi-agent systems that aggregate subagent outputs can be manipulated by a few malicious agents, so aggregation rules and agent trust need security design.

items.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
items.summary: GeneFlow is a framework for predicting expression of large gene panels from histology images, presented as a simpler and more efficient alternative to complex existing methods.

items.title: Condensing Law of Security Information
items.summary: The paper argues that the scaling-law assumption that larger LLMs always do better fails in security, because anomalous, long-tailed inputs such as zero-day attacks are poorly served by likelihood fitting.
items.why: Engineers choosing models for security tasks should not assume bigger models will detect rare anomalies better.

items.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
items.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design for real-world mineral exploration.

items.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
items.summary: The paper audits the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, finding run-to-run score variation and classifying failures by which layer's owner would fix them.
items.why: Shows that leaderboard scores hide instability and cost variation in agents, and that failures need ownership-based diagnosis before deployment.

items.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
items.summary: Researchers introduce G-CGEC, a task and benchmark for correcting grammatical errors in handwritten Chinese essay images by predicting both corrections and their positions.
items.why: Image-grounded correction for handwritten K-12 essays extends grammar-correction systems beyond digital text, a gap for education products.

items.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
items.summary: RL^RT is an on-device reinforcement learning runtime that shares one embedded GPU between an actor and learner, using a tunable refresh bound and GPU permits, evaluated on Jetson boards.
items.why: Engineers running RL on edge hardware face a tradeoff between actor stalls and policy drift, and this runtime makes that coupling tunable.

items.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
items.summary: TelePhysica is a closed-loop framework that reconstructs physically interactive 3D scenes from a single photograph, aiming for stable, simulatable scenes that support interventions.

items.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
items.summary: AG-JEPA adds anatomical tokens to a joint embedding predictive architecture to learn brain MRI representations for detecting early Alzheimer's-related changes.

items.title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
items.summary: EcoVGGT proposes pinned-key inference, choosing a few dozen evenly spread frames as attention keys for feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos, tested on VGGT and π³.
items.why: It targets the quadratic cost of cross-frame attention in multi-view transformers, suggesting a cheaper, streamable path for long-video 3D reconstruction.

items.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model
items.summary: An in-silico audit tests whether the TRIBE v2 brain-response model reproduces classic topographic organization such as retinotopy, tonotopy, and MT+ motion selectivity.

items.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
items.summary: Researchers introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), where an LLM agent builds transparent models by writing their weights and features in code, applied to transformers and brain encoding models.
items.why: It offers a route to interpretable models built by LLM agents, relevant to teams needing explainable predictive systems.

items.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
items.summary: PUMA-Former is proposed as an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative computation offloading across MEO-LEO satellite networks with incomplete CPU state information.

items.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
items.summary: The paper studies task-conditioned persona selection, composing LLM trading agent panels based on task characteristics, and instantiates it as FinPanel.
items.why: It suggests multi-agent LLM systems should select roles per task rather than reuse a fixed cast, a design choice relevant to agent architects.

items.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
items.summary: T2ST is a data-efficient training framework that augments scarce spatio-temporal data with abundant time-series data to build spatio-temporal foundation models.
items.why: It offers a way to train spatio-temporal foundation models when synchronized observations and spatial metadata are scarce.

items.title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification
items.summary: An introductory paper presents the Lean 4 proof assistant for system identification and control audiences, showing how machine-checked proofs can verify scientific derivations.

items.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
items.summary: The paper examines how personal LLM-powered assistant robots could be personalized to individual users' basic and moral value profiles rather than an aggregate human value set.
items.why: Shows that per-user value alignment for assistant robots may differ from single aggregate alignment targets, relevant to product design.

items.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
items.summary: RACE proposes ranking-uncertainty aware, capacity-adaptive model compression for sequential recommendation, varying compression by user intent complexity instead of uniform ratios.
items.why: It offers a way to allocate compute in recommenders by request complexity rather than applying one compression ratio everywhere.

items.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
items.summary: ParetoM³ proposes a penalty-based min-max-min formulation for preference-guided learning on the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives.

items.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
items.summary: The paper presents a method to acquire per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU LLM process using a non-modifying debugger, enabling request-level attribution.
items.why: It enables forensic analysis of running LLM services that cannot be restarted or modified, useful for incident investigation in production.

items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
items.summary: The paper proposes trajectory-aware activation steering for LLMs, treating steering with sparse autoencoders as a per-token allocation problem under a fixed budget of steerable tokens.
items.why: It suggests when steering is applied during generation affects output quality, offering a way to control behavior with less degradation.

items.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
items.summary: PrivacyPR is a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests linking real privacy defects and fixes, built to benchmark whether coding agents catch GDPR-relevant issues in code review.
items.why: It provides a benchmark for testing whether AI code review tools catch privacy defects, relevant to compliance-focused engineering teams.

items.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
items.summary: The paper explores whether oracle models can predict quantum runtime and approximation error to select configuration parameters for sample-based quantum diagonalization.

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.summary: A position piece argues that agentic robotics, where a foundation model runs a closed loop of observing, reasoning, invoking skills, and verifying, is replacing task-specific robot policies.
items.why: It frames a shift from dedicated robot policies to foundation-model agents, though the piece's claims about a specific release are unverified here.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
items.summary: A survey reviews 88 vision-language-action (VLA) robot models from December 2022 to October 2026, covering design, training, and deployment across manipulation, navigation, and humanoid control.
items.why: It offers a life-cycle reference for engineers building robot foundation models, from architecture choices through training and deployment.

items.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
items.summary: Researchers propose an AI method for synthesizing multi-view echocardiographic images using dynamic shape control, aiming to reduce reliance on scarce annotated clinical datasets.

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.summary: Gamer is a generalist vision-language-action agent framework for long-horizon tasks in 2D graphical interfaces and 3D simulated worlds, trained on keyboard and mouse interaction data.
items.why: Unified agents that operate across game and embodied environments show how perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning can be combined in one pipeline.

items.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
items.summary: CoPre-MoE proposes a mixture-of-experts method for multimodal continual instruction tuning that aims to reduce cross-task redundancy and parameter growth while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
items.why: Addresses parameter growth in continually updated multimodal models, a practical cost concern for teams fine-tuning MLLMs over time.

items.title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
items.summary: A participatory workshop with 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners examined how EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems translate into technical requirements and compliance evidence.
items.why: Shows where interpretation gaps arise when turning EU AI Act obligations into measurable technical compliance evidence.

items.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
items.summary: Researchers introduce a black-box two-level ensemble method for LLM uncertainty quantification that aims to separate aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty without white-box access.
items.why: Lets teams using closed LLM APIs distinguish prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps, improving reliability signals without model internals.

items.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
items.summary: The paper introduces Verification Transport, a test measuring whether LLM verifier judgments of agent executions remain correct when trajectories are abstracted, composed, or compacted.
items.why: Agent evaluators may give different verdicts once tool composition or history compaction hides evidence, affecting how teams trust automated agent checks.

items.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
items.summary: A scoping review finds AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is moving toward agentic systems, but most remain human-led and embodied healthcare robotics stays mostly at prototype or pilot stage.
items.why: Indicates that autonomous care agents with real decision-action coupling are still largely experimental, guiding realistic healthcare deployment planning.

items.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
items.summary: The paper studies interactive program induction, using language model priors to resolve ambiguity when recovering a program from a few input-output examples.

items.title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
items.summary: TradeGauntlet is a replayable limit-order-book simulator that evaluates compliance controls for autonomous trading agents, testing 1,680 sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.
items.why: Demonstrates how pre-trade gates and reminders trade off detection, prevention, and execution cost for agents operating under compliance constraints.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Researchers formulate fault-tolerant quantum circuit design as agentic evolutionary search, aiming to automate circuits for logical state preparation and gates that are now mostly hand-designed.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.summary: MeReader is a privacy-preserving, offline AI assistant for eBook reading that limits retrieval and generation to the reader's current position to avoid narrative spoilers.
items.why: Illustrates a local-first RAG design that restricts context by reading progress, relevant to privacy-sensitive consumer deployments.

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: The paper introduces a framework for jointly designing interpolant schedules and ODE discretization for generative models based on analyticity, with a conformal-mapping solution for Gaussians.

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: WeightBench is a benchmark evaluating LLMs on 42 weight-space programming tasks across reading, fixing, and writing neural network weights without gradient descent.
items.why: Provides a standard way to measure whether LLMs can directly read and edit other networks' parameters, an emerging capability.

items.title: From Chats to Markets: AgenticPay for LLM-Powered Negotiation in Multi-Agent Commerce
items.summary: AgenticPay is a benchmark with 160 multimodal tasks across four commerce scenarios and eight market topologies for evaluating LLM agents negotiating multi-issue agreements in competitive markets.
items.why: Gives teams a testbed for assessing how autonomous agents negotiate and transact in multi-agent markets before deploying them commercially.

items.title: Evaluating Chain-of-Thought Reasoning through Reusability and Verifiability
items.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning passed between a Sender LLM and a Receiver LLM is reliable, useful, and safe.
items.why: Multi-model pipelines pass reasoning traces downstream, so engineers need to know whether that transferred reasoning can be trusted and acted on.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Large Language Models with Incoherence-adjusted Semantic Volume
items.summary: Researchers introduce UMPIRE, a training-free uncertainty quantification framework for multimodal LLMs intended to flag unreliable outputs.
items.why: Reliable uncertainty signals could let teams route risky multimodal queries to human experts or larger models without extra training.

items.title: Multi-Environment POMDPs with Finite-Horizon Objectives
items.summary: Researchers study computing optimal values and policies for multi-environment POMDPs with finite-horizon objectives, where the initial state is adversarially chosen.

items.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
items.summary: Researchers treat LLM persona vectors as dynamic probes, tracking their alignment with hidden activations during reasoning across four open-weight models.
items.why: Monitoring persona signals during generation could offer a way to observe and steer model behavior mid-reasoning rather than only statically.

items.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers present D-VLA, a distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework for training Vision-Language-Action models at high concurrency.
items.why: Addresses throughput bottlenecks from balancing physical simulation against VRAM and bandwidth demands when running RL on large VLA models.

items.title: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
items.summary: Researchers present ShopGym, a framework for simulating and benchmarking e-commerce web agents in reproducible, scalable environments.
items.why: Offers a controllable alternative to live storefronts for evaluating shopping agents, which teams building web agents need for repeatable comparisons.

items.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
items.summary: Researchers propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling for nested contextual causal bandits, where a strategic decision shapes the context for later tactical choices.

items.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
items.summary: Researchers introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark where six LLM coding agents run farmers, roasters, and retailers in a simulated coffee supply chain.
items.why: Shows a way to test long-horizon multi-agent business behavior in simulated economies, relevant to assessing agents before deploying them in business roles.

items.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
items.summary: Researchers propose a regression-free, layout-aware matching method to reduce coordinate hallucinations in visual MLLM-based GUI grounding.
items.why: Coordinate hallucinations are a practical reliability problem for screenshot-based GUI agents that must click precise elements.

items.title: ReForge: Keeping ABR Algorithms Never Finished with Verified Large Language Model Revisions
items.summary: Researchers propose ReForge, which revises ABR video streaming algorithms with verified LLM edits after deployment without degrading performance on networks already served.
items.why: Shows a path to continuously improving deployed networking policies with LLMs while guarding against regressions on existing conditions.

items.title: Programmable Distributions of Semantics-Preserving Variants for Evaluating Code Agents
items.summary: Researchers evaluate coding agents on semantically equivalent rewrites of repositories, finding resolve rates can shift under superficial code variations.
items.why: Suggests coding agent benchmarks may overstate reliability, since behavior can change when code is rewritten without altering its meaning.

items.title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry
items.summary: A critical evaluation examines using LLMs to help create EU regulatory compliance artifacts such as Digital Product Passports and GDPR impact assessments in industry.
items.why: Gives compliance and engineering leaders evidence on how far LLM-assisted documentation can meet EU requirements in practice.

items.title: AI Agents Push Humans Out of the Loop
items.summary: A position paper argues current AI agent designs undermine effective human oversight and degrade the cognitive capacities oversight requires.
items.why: Challenges the assumption that keeping a human in the loop is sufficient, which affects how teams design agent oversight.

items.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-Agent Interaction
items.summary: Researchers propose efficient test-time adaptation via iterative human-agent interaction to capture criteria users cannot fully specify upfront.
items.why: Suggests a way to tailor agent outputs to individual expert standards through repeated interaction rather than upfront specification.

items.title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
items.summary: Researchers introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a reward fine-tuning objective for few-step average-velocity generators that matches the inference-time average-velocity map.

items.title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers describe the CKG Clinical Explanation Engine, which turns knowledge-graph reasoning outputs into typed facts, rule traces, and provenance-linked clinical recommendations.
items.why: It targets auditable clinical decision support, where engineers building healthcare systems need traceable links from observations to recommendations.

items.title: When to Rethink: Learning Multi-Perspective Self-Verification for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-perspective self-verification method for vision-language models to better detect plausible but incorrect answers without external judges.
items.why: More reliable self-verification could reduce wrong answers from multimodal systems without adding external judge models.

items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.summary: Researchers introduce a self-building laboratory that designs, configures, and operates its own lab setup from a high-level scientific goal.

items.title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
items.summary: Google and Meta describe TorchTPU, an open-source native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs supporting eager execution and torch.compile integration.
items.why: Engineers running PyTorch can migrate models to TPUs with less rework, using a native backend rather than a separate port.

items.title: FlashRT-PAI: Fast Kernels Are Not Fast Pipelines for Physical AI
items.summary: FlashRT-PAI targets real-time inference latency in physical AI models, arguing system-level overhead, not kernel speed, dominates vision-language-action pipelines.
items.why: Robotics teams optimizing real-time inference may find kernel-level speedups insufficient without addressing pipeline overhead.

items.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
items.summary: A survey proposes a two-layer taxonomy for pluralistic alignment in LLMs, separating target behavior, whose preferences define the reference, and evidence of success.

items.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
items.summary: TimesJev proposes using fast System 1 models for time series reasoning, aiming to avoid the thousands of tokens long chain-of-thought reasoning requires.
items.why: Reducing reasoning tokens could cut inference latency for time series applications that currently depend on long chain-of-thought outputs.

items.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
items.summary: A controlled study examines whether LLMs can improve their own harness, the scaffold orchestrating model calls, on the ARC-AGI-3 interactive benchmark.
items.why: Self-improving agent scaffolds bear on how much human engineering agent harnesses will require in future.

items.title: One Offset, Two Directions: Baseline Adjustment via Subgroup Offsets
items.summary: Researchers propose subgroup-based baseline adjustment for GRPO, arguing the global within-prompt mean baseline collapses heterogeneous rollout subgroups with distinct rewards.
items.why: Better advantage baselines could improve reinforcement learning fine-tuning of reasoning models that use GRPO.

items.title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
items.summary: Researchers show visual readers of neural field weights can be highly accurate on original weights yet sensitive to function-preserving equivalent representations.

items.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
items.summary: AttentionSwitch proposes a jailbreak defense for LLMs that jointly learns sparse attention-head selection and scaling, avoiding costly fine-tuning.
items.why: Targeted component interventions offer a potentially cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for hardening LLMs against jailbreaks.

items.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
items.summary: ABHBench is a multimodal benchmark built from the game Detroit: Become Human that tests how foundation models make moral decisions as acting agents.
items.why: Evaluating models as first-person agents exposes moral behavior that third-person vignette benchmarks miss, relevant to autonomous deployments.

items.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: Sage-Taiyi is a metacognition-inspired architecture that guides scientific investigation, reporting first place on all eight metrics of the Taiyi-Bench ideation benchmark.

items.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
items.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline that generates data visualisation embedding algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities.
items.why: Shows agents automating algorithm design for user-specified objectives, a pattern applicable to other engineering tooling.

items.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
items.summary: MIGRO is a decoupled long-term memory system that keeps interaction history as persistent state shared across successive language models.
items.why: A model-independent memory layer could let teams swap underlying LLMs without losing accumulated user context.

items.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
items.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which read text with a language model and output calibrated yes/no, choice, or graded-score decisions.
items.why: Typed decision heads could cut inference cost for routing and classification, but the text gives few concrete results to judge them by.

items.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
items.summary: Researchers present a toolkit that profiles LLM risk propensities, measuring how risk-averse or consistent models are across contexts and generations.
items.why: Standardized risk profiles could help teams predict model behavior and compare model generations before deploying them in sensitive settings.

items.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
items.summary: S1-Evo proposes a self-evolving attack framework that manipulates typed System-1 decision models used for routing, moderation, and authorization in LLM agents.
items.why: Agents relying on typed decision models for authorization may be vulnerable to context-based manipulation, so these attacks matter for defense design.

items.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
items.summary: Ballad uses bandit-based routing across LLMs for automated heuristic discovery, finding no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models on NP-hard problems.
items.why: Engineers may be able to cut costs in automated optimization pipelines by routing among cheaper models rather than always using the most expensive one.

items.title: Fake News Detectors are Biased against Texts Generated by Large Language Models
items.summary: A study finds many fake news detectors are biased, more often flagging LLM-generated texts as fake than human-written ones.
items.why: Teams using automated detectors to filter content should check for bias against machine-generated text, since it can skew moderation outcomes.

items.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
items.summary: Astraios is a suite of 28 instruction-tuned code models comparing seven parameter-efficient tuning methods across four model sizes up to 16 billion parameters.
items.why: The comparison of tuning methods across scales helps engineers pick cost-effective fine-tuning approaches for code models.

items.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions
items.summary: BigCodeBench is a benchmark testing code generation that uses diverse function calls and complex instructions, beyond short algorithmic tasks.
items.why: It offers a more realistic test of whether code models can use multiple tools for practical tasks, informing model selection.

items.title: Benign Overfitting for Regression with Trained Two-Layer ReLU Networks
items.summary: A theoretical paper proves generalization results for two-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient flow in the neural tangent kernel regime.

items.title: LEGAL-UQA: Testing Constitutional Question-Answering Systems for Urdu Speakers with a Parallel English-Urdu Benchmark
items.summary: LEGAL-UQA is a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs based on Pakistan's Constitution, for testing constitutional question answering.
items.why: It shows how multilingual legal assistants need language-specific evaluation data, which teams building non-English RAG systems should account for.

items.title: AbFlowNet: Optimizing Antibody-Antigen Binding Energy via Diffusion-GFlowNet Fusion
items.summary: AbFlowNet combines diffusion and GFlowNet methods to jointly optimize antibody CDR design for antigen binding energy.

items.title: Chi-Square Wavelet Graph Neural Networks for Heterogeneous Graph Anomaly Detection
items.summary: ChiGAD is a spectral graph neural network framework for anomaly detection in heterogeneous graphs, addressing meta-path semantics and class imbalance.

items.title: Graph Your Own Prompt
items.summary: Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR) injects relational graph structure derived from model predictions into training to produce more class-aware representations.

items.title: BigCodeArena: Unveiling More Reliable Human Preferences in Code Generation via Execution
items.summary: BigCodeArena is an open human evaluation platform for code generation that runs generated code on the fly so raters can judge execution results.
